pairs: Addens quoque Eliu,
Continuing in a similar manner,
hæc locutus est:
Eliu had this to say:
Sustine me paululum,
Bear with me for a little while
et indicabo tibi:
and I will show you;
adhuc enim habeo quod pro Deo loquar.
for I have still more to say in favor of God.
Repetam scientiam meam a principio,
I will review my knowledge from the beginning,
et operatorem meum probabo justum.
and I will prove my Maker to be just.
Vere enim absque mendacio sermones mei,
For truly my words are without any falsehood
et perfecta scientia probabitur tibi.
and perfect knowledge will be proven to you.
Deus potentes non abjicit,
God does not abandon the powerful,
cum et ipse sit potens:
for he himself is also powerful.
sed non salvat impios,
But he does not save the impious,
et judicium pauperibus tribuit.
though he grants judgment to the poor.
Non auferet a justo oculos suos:
He will not take his eyes away from the just,
et reges in solio collocat in perpetuum,
and he continually establishes kings on their throne,
et illi eriguntur.
and they are exalted.
Et si fuerint in catenis,
And, if they are in captivity,
et vinciantur funibus paupertatis,
or are bound with the chains of poverty,
indicabit eis opera eorum,
he will reveal to them their works,
et scelera eorum,
as well as their sinfulness,
quia violenti fuerunt.
in that they were violent.
Revelabit quoque aurem eorum,
Likewise,
ut corripiat:
he will open their ears to his correction,
et loquetur,
and he will speak to them,
ut revertantur ab iniquitate.
so that they may return from iniquity.
Si audierint et observaverint,
If they listen and obey,
complebunt dies suos in bono, et annos suos in gloria:
they will fill their days with goodness and complete their years in glory.
si autem non audierint,
But if they will not listen,
transibunt per gladium,
they will pass away by the sword
et consumentur in stultitia.
and will be consumed by foolishness.
Simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei,
The false and the crafty provoke the wrath of God,
neque clamabunt cum vincti fuerint.
yet they do not cry out to him when they are chained.
Morietur in tempestate anima eorum,
Their soul will die in a storm,
et vita eorum inter effeminatos.
and their life, among the unmanly.
Eripiet de angustia sua pauperem,
He will rescue the poor from his anguish,
et revelabit in tribulatione aurem ejus.
and he will open his ear during tribulation.
Igitur salvabit te de ore angusto latissime,
Therefore, he will save you from the narrow mouth very widely,
et non habente fundamentum subter se:
even though it has no foundation under it.
requies autem mensæ tuæ erit plena pinguedine.
Moreover, your respite at table will be full of fatness.
Causa tua quasi impii judicata est:
Your case has been judged like that of the impious;
causam judiciumque recipies.
you will withdraw your plea and your judgment.
Non te ergo superet ira ut aliquem opprimas:
Therefore, do not let anger overwhelm you so that you oppress another;
nec multitudo donorum inclinet te.
neither should you allow a multitude of gifts to influence you.
Depone magnitudinem tuam absque tribulatione,
Lay down your greatness without distress,
et omnes robustos fortitudine.
and put aside all of your power with courage.
Ne protrahas noctem,
Do not prolong the night,
ut ascendant populi pro eis.
even if people rise on their behalf.
Cave ne declines ad iniquitatem:
Be careful that you do not turn to iniquity;
hanc enim cœpisti sequi post miseriam.
for, after your misery, you have begun to follow this.
Ecce Deus excelsus in fortitudine sua,
Behold, God is exalted in his strength,
et nullus ei similis in legislatoribus.
and there is no one like him among the law-givers.
Quis poterit scrutari vias ejus? aut quis potest ei dicere:
Who is able to investigate his ways? And who can say,
Operatus es iniquitatem?
“You have done iniquity,” to him?
Memento quod ignores opus ejus,
Remember that you are ignorant of his work,
de quo cecinerunt viri.
yet men have sung its praises.
Omnes homines vident eum:
All men consider him;
unusquisque intuetur procul.
and each one ponders from a distance.
Ecce Deus magnus vincens scientiam nostram:
Behold, God is great, defeating our knowledge;
numerus annorum ejus inæstimabilis.
the number of his years is inestimable.
Qui aufert stillas pluviæ,
He carries away the drops of rain,
et effundit imbres ad instar gurgitum,
and he sends forth showers like a raging whirlpool;
qui de nubibus fluunt quæ prætexunt cuncta desuper.
they flow from the clouds that are woven above everything.
Si voluerit extendere nubes quasi tentorium suum,
If he wills it, he extends the clouds as his tent
et fulgurare lumine suo desuper,
and shines with his light from above; likewise,
cardines quoque maris operiet.
he covers the oceans within his tent.
Per hæc enim judicat populos,
For he judges the people by these things,
et dat escas multis mortalibus.
and he gives food to a multitude of mortals.
In manibus abscondit lucem,
Within his hands, he hides the light,
et præcepit ei ut rursus adveniat.
and he commands it to come forth again.
Annuntiat de ea amico suo,
He announces it to his friend,
quod possessio ejus sit,
for it is his possession
et ad eam possit ascendere.
and he is able to reach out to it.
